newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot market remains sluggish.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot market remains sluggish.

text.p: Differentials held mostly steady this week on the New York physical coffee market even as CSCE futures prices climbed, but spot business remained exceedingly light, traders said.

Since last Friday, CSCE's nearby September contract has risen 12.00 cents -- or about seven percent, with September's premium to second-month December bulging to more than 20.00 cents during the week.
"There's virtually no business on the spot market," said one trader. "If you don't absolutely need coffee, you're not going to buy against September."
"Besides, it is summer and business is slow," he added.
Colombian spreads did show some signs of easing this week in relation to the spike in futures prices, but were still considered relatively pricey.

Spot Colombian MAMs netted 23 cents over "C" compared with 25 cents over last week. MAMS for September delivery, which were heard at 15 cents over December earlier this week, garnered 16 to 17 cents over by the week's end.
Elsewhere, spot Mexican beans were steady at even to one cent over "C". Spot Indian Plantation Bs, which did not pass exchange certification, were heard at five cents over "C".

Much of the discussion this week centered on exchange certified coffee stocks. Traders noted that about 65 percent of coffee graded failed to pass CSCE approval. Additionally, there was talk that some members of the trade were unhappy with the quality of some of certified coffee stocks from Africa.

Meanwhile, U.S. roasters Folgers and Maxwell House said earlier this week they would cut the wholesale prices on their standard 13-ounce cans of ground regular and ground decaffeinated coffees by 30 cents due to the futures market sharp decline from 20-year highs in late May.
The decrease, which does not take effect until September 8, brings the price for a standard 13-ounce can of regular ground coffee to $3.06, and decaffeinated coffee to $3.76.
CSCE September coffee fell 4.10 cents a lb Friday to settle at 176.30. December ended 3.05 cents lower at 157.25.
